prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: Earth-observation mission (land/coastal/cryosphere). Ground segment plans, acquires, operates, processes, archives, gives access; spacecraft, launch, user processing out of scope. Elements: Mission Control Center (MCC, alias Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands, owns contact schedule, primary routing policy point; contacts have readiness check, live monitoring, post-pass closure. Flight Dynamics Facility (FDF, alias Mistral): orbit, maneuvers; sends visibility predictions, antenna pointing products to planning. Payload Processing Facility (PPF, alias Forgehouse): processing, calibration, distribution; Primary (nominal) and Backup (failover, routinely tested) Processing Clusters; archive transfers rate-limited during contacts. Network Control System (alias Lantern): authoritative WAN status; station allocations, antenna readiness, contact times; screens timing alarms before forwarding to Spacecraft Operations Team; sends MCC antenna status, link config, timing references, routing readiness pre-pass. Mission Planning System: receives booking requests. Command Validation Gateway: rule-checks plans, executes console-lead-authorized commands. Telemetry Ingest Service: accepts real-time frames, validates framing/time continuity, records reception metadata; produces Pass Replay Packet post-contact for engineering review. Orbit Determination Engine: Doppler Residual Report per pass; state updates, basis for visibility, maneuver constraints, pointing. Product Quality Service; User Services Portal. Antennas: North S-Band (nominal uplink), South S-Band (alternate) for command/low-rate telemetry to MCC via protected routers; Kiruna, Svalbard X-Band high-rate telemetry when geometry/volume justify, dual WAN to PPF; sites validate time. Actors: Spacecraft Operations Team monitors mode, power, thermal, attitude, command counters, storage, fault messages on MCC consoles (deviation-focused): console lead declares pass status, authorizes commands, pauses on mismatch; telemetry engineer checks quality, frame loss, latency, continuity; spacecraft systems engineer checks flight rules, records anomaly context. Ground Network Manager (alias Juniper): antenna assignment, link availability, site coordination, conflicts, Antenna Deicing Notice, pins critical paths pre-AOS; latency breach diagnosis; consults Cybersecurity Desk (Security Exception Ticket; per-shift reviews) before blocking. Flight Dynamics Team: tracking + time tags for orbit assessment, timing quality. Payload Calibration Team. Pass reconstruction after close: command history, telemetry timing, station status, logs into narrative;

New part:
S093: The Mission Control Center coordinates with the Payload Processing Facility when instrument mode changes, data downlink priorities, or reception gaps could affect downstream processing.
S094: The Payload Calibration Team sends the Calibration Patch Bundle after calibration analysis identifies an approved update for payload processing behavior.
S095: Subsystem specialists are not expected to staff every live contact, but they must be reachable during planned critical activities and whenever a console operator declares an off-nominal condition.
S096: Escalation from the Mission Control Center begins with the console lead, moves to the responsible discipline lead, and then reaches mission management when the condition threatens spacecraft safety, contact continuity, or recovery schedule.
S097: The Spacecraft Operations Team and Flight Dynamics Team coordinate closely before orbit-control activities so that command timing, attitude constraints, tracking expectations, and post-burn assessment steps remain consistent.
S098: When telemetry indicates a possible onboard fault, operators preserve the command state, avoid discretionary commanding, and request specialist review before changing spacecraft configuration.
S099: The Mission Planning System receives operational constraints from mission control after anomalies, station outages, or spacecraft configuration changes require adjustment of future contacts or payload activities.
S100: At the end of each shift, the Mission Control Center records unresolved actions, open engineering questions, and expected specialist responses so that the next operations crew can maintain continuity without relying on informal handover.
S101: Mission planning begins when observation requests arrive through the User Services Portal or from internal operations channels at the Mission Control Center.
S102: The Mission Planning System, also called Cedar in this section, is the authoritative tool for assembling candidate observation timelines and associated ground contact activities.
S103: Each request is checked for requester authority, target definition, time sensitivity, acquisition mode, expected data volume, and any handling restrictions before it is admitted to the planning pool.
S104: The User Services Portal records the request state so that external users can distinguish accepted requests from those still awaiting technical review.
S105: The Spacecraft Operations Team reviews late operational requests when they affect spacecraft attitude, thermal margin, stored command capacity, or contact preparation.
S106: The Flight Dynamics Facility provides orbit predictions and visibility assumptions that the planning cycle uses to determine feasible imaging windows and ground contacts.
S107: The Mission Planning System combines request priority, instrument availability, contact opportunities, onboard storage margin, and downlink capacity into a draft activity schedule.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
